source: 5 AAC 30 (Yakutat Area), Article 2 (Fishing districts) and Article 3 (Salmon fishery); the corresponding printed booklet is the 2025-2028 Southeastern Alaska/Yakutat Areas Commercial Salmon Fishing Regulations
citation: 5 AAC 30.200 (fishing districts); 5 AAC 30.350 (closed waters); 5 AAC 30.310 (fishing seasons, for the only coordinate attached to the Situk-Ahrnklin Inlet); 5 AAC 30.365 (Situk-Ahrnklin Inlet and Lost River King Salmon Fisheries Management Plan)
notation: degrees and decimal minutes, e.g. "59° 20.83' N. lat." / "139° 59.35' W. long." -- NOT degrees-minutes-seconds. lat_dm/lon_dm hold the value EXACTLY as printed, unconverted, including the source's inconsistent degree sign: 5 AAC 30.200 and 5 AAC 30.350(a)(5) and (a)(9) print º (U+00BA, masculine ordinal) while 5 AAC 30.310, 30.350(a)(13) and 30.365 print ° (U+00B0). Several values are printed as whole degrees or whole minutes with no decimal -- Cape Suckling "144º W. long.", Icy Cape "141º 42' W. long.", the Yakutat Bay line "59° 40' N. lat." -- and are recorded that way. Cape Suckling will not parse as degrees+minutes. Decimal conversion is degrees + minutes/60, negative for west longitude.
source_document_caveat: The ADF&G booklet named in source_url could not be read directly: this session's fetch relay returns only summaries of PDFs and direct download is blocked by network policy. All text here was transcribed from two published mirrors of the codified regulation -- Cornell LII and Justia -- listed in text_retrieved_from. Both derive from the same state codification, so their agreement proves faithful transcription, not independent authority. CURRENCY DIFFERS BY HOST: Cornell's History note for 5 AAC 30.350 ends "am 6/27/2025, Register 254, July 2025" and for 5 AAC 30.365 ends the same, while Justia's chapter 30 pages are "current through November 28, 2024". Where the two differ, Cornell is the later text and is what is recorded, with the divergence written into that area's notes. Any Board of Fisheries amendment after June 2025, and any emergency order, is NOT reflected here. Verify against the printed booklet before fishing.
verification_method: Every area was read at least twice by differently-worded fetches, in almost every case across two different hosts (Cornell LII and Justia). Only values identical in both reads carry verified_twice=true. Two areas carry verified_twice=false and say why in their notes: 5 AAC 30.350(a)(13) (Sudden Stream/Malaspina Lake) exists only in Cornell's post-2025 text, and 5 AAC 30.365's troll box differs between hosts for the same vintage reason. Every decimal value was recomputed by hand as degrees + minutes/60, negated for west longitude, and checked against the Yakutat envelope lat 58.5-61, lon -145 to -137; every value fell inside it. No coordinate in this file came from any source other than the two mirrors; landmarks named without a printed coordinate carry lat_dm/lon_dm = null even where the same landmark's coordinate appears in another paragraph.
structure_notes: 5 AAC 30.200 has exactly TWO lettered subsections, (a) Yakataga District and (b) Yakutat District, and NO numbered sections or subsections inside either -- confirmed on both hosts. There is therefore no section-level geometry to extract for the Yakutat Area. 5 AAC 30.350 is "Closed waters": subsection (a) is a flat list (1)-(13), subsection (b) was repealed 10/1/1998, and subsection (c) defines "mean low water" as "the average of the low tides of that day". THREE OF THE FOUR NAMED TARGETS HAVE NO COORDINATES IN REGULATION: the Situk-Ahrnklin Inlet, the Kaliakh River and the Seal River. The phrase "Seal River" does not appear anywhere in 5 AAC chapter 30 -- checked in 30.310, 30.340, 30.345 and 30.350 -- so the Yakataga District's Seal River set gillnet fishery has no regulatory boundary of its own and falls under the district description in 5 AAC 30.200(a) and the emergency-order season in 5 AAC 30.310(a)(1) ("in the Yakataga District the opening and closing dates will be established by emergency order").

areas.notes: THE SITUK-AHRNKLIN INLET HAS NO COORDINATE BOUNDARY IN REGULATION. Every section of 5 AAC 30 that names the inlet -- 30.310 (fishing seasons), 30.345 (two units of set gillnet gear), 30.350 (closed waters) and 30.365 (Situk-Ahrnklin Inlet and Lost River King Salmon Fisheries Management Plan) -- refers to it by name only. The single coordinate in 5 AAC 30.310 is the 59° 40' N. lat. line that splits Yakutat Bay between paragraphs (B) and (C); it is NOT the inlet's boundary. Printed as whole minutes with no decimal in both reads.

HOSTS DISAGREE: Justia prints the northern intersection as 59° 28.65' N. lat., 139° 51.17' W. long. and the southern line as running from 59° 20.30' N. lat., 139° 16.50' W. long. to 59° 18.25' N. lat., 139° 21.94' W. long., and labels 59° 30.49' N. lat., 139° 46.58' W. long. as "(Ocean Cape)". The divergence is a vintage difference, not a transcription error: Cornell's History note for this section ends "am 6/27/2025, Register 254, July 2025" while Justia's page is "current through November 28, 2024". The values recorded here are Cornell's post-amendment values, confirmed by three differently-worded Cornell reads that agreed digit for digit.
